# rubrik_data_security_policy (Resource)

The `rubrik_data_security_policy` resource is used to create and manage data
security policies in RSC.

A policy matches on up to two groups of conditions: object conditions, in the
`object_filter` block, and identity conditions, in the `identity_filter` block.
At least one of the two blocks is required. Conditions within a block are joined
by the block's `op` field, and the two blocks are always joined by AND. This is
the only filter shape RSC accepts, and it mirrors the RSC data security policy
editor.

Which block a condition belongs to follows from its `filter_type`:
`SECURITY_DOCUMENT_*` and `SECURITY_SNAPPABLE_*` conditions are object
conditions, `SECURITY_IDENTITY_*` and `SECURITY_GPO_*` conditions are identity
conditions.

The optional `threshold_filter` block decides how many matches raise a
violation. It holds a single condition, matching the RSC data security policy
editor.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Policy matching highly sensitive documents in unprotected objects. A
# single object condition group is the simplest useful policy.
resource "rubrik_data_security_policy" "overexposed_sensitive_data" {
  name        = "Overexposed Sensitive Data"
  description = "Highly sensitive documents without backup protection"
  category    = "OVEREXPOSED"
  severity    = "CRITICAL"

  object_filter {
    op = "AND"

    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_DOCUMENT_SENSITIVITY"
      values       = ["HIGH", "MEDIUM"]
      relationship = "IS"
    }

    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_SNAPPABLE_BACKUP"
      values       = ["Unprotected"]
      relationship = "IS"
    }
  }
}

# Policy combining object and identity conditions. The two blocks are
# always joined by AND, while the conditions inside each block are joined
# by the block's op field.
resource "rubrik_data_security_policy" "exposed_to_service_accounts" {
  name        = "Sensitive Data Exposed To Service Accounts"
  description = "Sensitive documents reachable by service accounts"
  category    = "OVEREXPOSED"
  severity    = "HIGH"

  object_filter {
    op = "OR"

    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_DOCUMENT_SENSITIVITY"
      values       = ["HIGH"]
      relationship = "IS"
    }

    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_SNAPPABLE_ENCRYPTION"
      values       = ["ENCRYPTION_DISABLED"]
      relationship = "IS"
    }
  }

  identity_filter {
    op = "AND"

    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_IDENTITY_NAME"
      values       = ["svc-"]
      relationship = "CONTAINS"
    }
  }
}

# Policy raising a violation only once enough documents match. The
# threshold filter is typically a hit count condition.
resource "rubrik_data_security_policy" "bulk_sensitive_data" {
  name        = "Bulk Sensitive Data"
  description = "Objects holding more than 100 highly sensitive documents"
  category    = "MISPLACED"
  severity    = "MEDIUM"
  enabled     = false

  object_filter {
    condition {
      filter_type  = "SECURITY_DOCUMENT_SENSITIVITY"
      values       = ["HIGH"]
      relationship = "IS"
    }
  }

  threshold_filter {
    filter_type  = "SECURITY_DOCUMENT_HIT_COUNT"
    values       = ["100"]
    relationship = "GREATER_THAN"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `category` (String) Category of the data security policy. Valid values are MISPLACED, OVEREXPOSED, REDUNDANT and UNPROTECTED.
- `name` (String) Name of the data security policy.
- `severity` (String) Severity of the data security policy. Valid values are LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the data security policy.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the data security policy is enabled.
- `identity_filter` (Block List) Identity conditions for the data security policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--identity_filter))
- `object_filter` (Block List) Object conditions for the data security policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--object_filter))
- `threshold_filter` (Block List) Threshold condition deciding how many matches raise a violation. Typically a SECURITY_DOCUMENT_HIT_COUNT condition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--threshold_filter))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data security policy ID (UUID).
- `predefined` (Boolean) Whether the data security policy is predefined.

<a id="nestedblock--identity_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `identity_filter`

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) Filter condition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--identity_filter--condition))
- `op` (String) Logical operator joining the conditions in this block. Valid values are AND and OR. Default value is AND.

<a id="nestedblock--identity_filter--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `identity_filter.condition`

Required:

- `filter_type` (String) Filter type. Valid filter types are SECURITY_IDENTITY_*, SECURITY_GPO_*.
- `relationship` (String) Comparison operator, e.g. IS, IS_NOT or CONTAINS. Which operators a filter type accepts depends on the filter type.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Filter values. Left out for a relationship taking no values, such as EXISTS, IS_EMPTY and IS_NOT_EMPTY. When specified, at least one value is required.



<a id="nestedblock--object_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `object_filter`

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) Filter condition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--object_filter--condition))
- `op` (String) Logical operator joining the conditions in this block. Valid values are AND and OR. Default value is AND.

<a id="nestedblock--object_filter--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `object_filter.condition`

Required:

- `filter_type` (String) Filter type. Valid filter types are SECURITY_DOCUMENT_*, SECURITY_SNAPPABLE_*.
- `relationship` (String) Comparison operator, e.g. IS, IS_NOT or CONTAINS. Which operators a filter type accepts depends on the filter type.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Filter values. Left out for a relationship taking no values, such as EXISTS, IS_EMPTY and IS_NOT_EMPTY. When specified, at least one value is required.



<a id="nestedblock--threshold_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `threshold_filter`

Required:

- `filter_type` (String) Filter type. Valid filter types are SECURITY_DOCUMENT_*, SECURITY_SNAPPABLE_*, SECURITY_IDENTITY_*, SECURITY_GPO_*.
- `relationship` (String) Comparison operator, e.g. IS, IS_NOT or CONTAINS. Which operators a filter type accepts depends on the filter type.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Filter values. Left out for a relationship taking no values, such as EXISTS, IS_EMPTY and IS_NOT_EMPTY. When specified, at least one value is required.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = rubrik_data_security_policy.policy
  identity = {
    id = "6ba9c3a1-2f4e-4d5c-9b1a-8e7f0d2c4a63"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Data security policy ID (UUID).

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = rubrik_data_security_policy.policy
  id = "6ba9c3a1-2f4e-4d5c-9b1a-8e7f0d2c4a63"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
% terraform import rubrik_data_security_policy.policy 6ba9c3a1-2f4e-4d5c-9b1a-8e7f0d2c4a63
```
